12 [...] Hi Product Hunt, I'm Shun, the maker of Ownfeed. I've shipped a few small products, and the same thing happened every time: I built it, I launched it, and nobody came. What did work was replying to people who were already describing the problem my product solves. But finding those posts ate up my whole day. So I built the thing I wanted: a feed, like a social timeline, where every post is from someone who might need my product. How it works: - Paste your product's URL. That's the whole setup, no keywords. - Ownfeed reads Reddit, X, Bluesky and Hacker News every day and keeps only the posts where your product can help. - Each post is tagged: Pain point, Looking for a tool, or Mention. - You scroll for five minutes each morning, open the original post, and reply. results.content: So I've incorporated RSS feeds of various types into multiple aspects of my life over the past 15 years, from keeping track of news, companies I've invested in, friends/social activity and more but this is by far the BEST RSS app I've come across and it's completely free. From creating custom feeds back in the early days of Feedburner for my own info-collection as well as to help propagate the marketing message of my clients then to hosting my own feed aggregators on my homelab to trying just about every type of RSS application in between including ones I've had to pay for, this one wins. It even made swapping over my well-curated and categorized feeds from my self-hosted freshrss install a literal 15 second process. But it's not just an RSS aggregator. It is literally an application that [...] phone and pick up exactly where I left off on my laptop. 5. Offline Reading is a Game-Changer Whether I’m on a plane or stuck in a subway with no internet, I can still access my saved articles. This feature has been a lifesaver. 6. You’re in Control Unlike social media platforms that decide what you see, Follow lets you choose your sources. It’s empowering to curate your own feed and escape the algorithm bubble. --- Cons 1. Limited Third-Party Integrations While it works great as a standalone app, integrating with tools like Pocket or Notion would make it even better for saving and organizing articles. 2. No Browser Extension A browser extension to quickly subscribe to RSS feeds would be a fantastic addition and make it even easier to use. 3. Might Feel Intimidating for New Users If [...] I used it for a few days now. My main use case is for following new articles from friends using RSS. I imported my OPML file. It took a while for articles to show up, but once it does it works really well. I love that the UI is very polished, IMO it's one of the most polished interface for reading feeds I've ever used. I also love that it supports many keyboard shortcuts and buttons have keyboard shortcuts intuitively shown in the tooltip. Do you have any plan for it to have a public API? I really would love to have the ability to subscribe to an OPML URL, because I manage my feed subscriptions in another system that provides a URL to an OPML file.
